questions.prompt: Which mental model best explains “Testing Generated CSS” in Dart Sass?
options: The browser executes Sass source directly, so a compilation step is unnecessary.
Readable SCSS guarantees correct browser rendering, accessibility, and performance without output review.
The best solution is always to replace native CSS behavior with a new Sass abstraction.

A stylesheet is correct only when it compiles and behaves correctly in the target browser and interface. Keep the source, compiler diagnostics, generated CSS, and rendered page available while debugging.
questions.answer_key: A stylesheet is correct only when it compiles and behaves correctly in the target browser and interface. Keep the source, compiler diagnostics, generated CSS, and rendered page available while debugging.
questions.explanation: A stylesheet is correct only when it compiles and behaves correctly in the target browser and interface. Keep the source, compiler diagnostics, generated CSS, and rendered page available while debugging. The alternative choices confuse Sass compilation with browser execution or claim guarantees that require independent tests.

questions.prompt: When applying “Reviewing compiled output”, which approach is the most reliable?
options: Prefer deeply nested selectors because fewer source lines always mean simpler and safer CSS.
Silence every warning before determining whether it identifies a deprecated or incorrect construct.
For reviewing compiled output, identify the relevant source rule, predict the intended result, and check the emitted CSS against that expectation.
Skip compilation and infer the final selector list and property values from the source file alone.
questions.answer_key: For reviewing compiled output, identify the relevant source rule, predict the intended result, and check the emitted CSS against that expectation.
questions.explanation: For reviewing compiled output, identify the relevant source rule, predict the intended result, and check the emitted CSS against that expectation. Compare the compiled output with the stated intent and preserve browser-native behavior where it is required.

questions.prompt: Which review decision most directly supports maintainability for “Testing Generated CSS”?
options: Expose internal implementation details as public API and postpone documentation until after release.

Use reproducible checks: compile the required entrypoints, inspect emitted selectors, test keyboard focus and reduced motion where relevant, and verify supported browser features independently of Sass syntax.
Generate every possible selector or theme combination, even when most variants are never used.
Treat successful compilation as proof that the interface is accessible and behaves correctly in every browser.
questions.answer_key: Use reproducible checks: compile the required entrypoints, inspect emitted selectors, test keyboard focus and reduced motion where relevant, and verify supported browser features independently of Sass syntax.
questions.explanation: Use reproducible checks: compile the required entrypoints, inspect emitted selectors, test keyboard focus and reduced motion where relevant, and verify supported browser features independently of Sass syntax. The other choices increase output, assume unverified behavior, or make the public interface harder to maintain.
